title: Fix stream 0 five-minute drops: dead gateway 192.168.28.1 on camera 0
description: Camera 0 (192.168.28.119) gateway points at nonexistent 192.168.28.1; firmware gateway health-check failure bounces network/streaming stack every ~298.5s, killing RTSP sessions. Fix: point gateway at live IP (192.168.28.8 NVR-1). Evidence: live probes 2026-06-12 (ICMP/HTTP blip + RST win0 + camera uptime 5.6d + ARP incomplete for 28.1; control cameras on live 27.1 never cycle).
close_reason: Root cause: camera 0 default gateway 192.168.28.1 nonexistent; firmware gateway health-check recovery bounced streaming stack every ~298.5s. Fixed by pointing gateway at 192.168.28.8 (NVR-1) via ISAPI + reboot at 19:09. Verified: 25+ min zero outages across 5 would-be cycles (previous all-day max: 5.2 min).

title: Make Stream 0 honor configured TCP permanently
description: Remove the Stream 0-only nvurisrcbin transport override that rewrites configured tcp to auto/multi, delete the temporary HICON_STREAM_0_NVURISRCBIN_RESPECT_CONFIGURED_PROTOCOL plumbing, keep outage instrumentation and soak tooling, and validate Stream 0 starts with requested=tcp effective=tcp plus a post-change soak.

title: Implement Stream 0 RTSP proof soak instrumentation
description: Add temporary runtime observability and soak tooling to prove whether Stream 0's recurring ~300s no-data/reconnect event is dominated by nvurisrcbin transport behavior, Jetson receive-buffer limits, or camera/path 192.168.28.119. Scope includes structured per-stream outage/recovery logs, an explicit Stream 0 nvurisrcbin transport override toggle, and a repeatable soak capture helper that collects journal evidence, tegrastats, NIC counters, and socket buffer state for baseline, forced-TCP, and forced-TCP-plus-buffer runs.

title: fix: nvurisrcbin FPS watchdog restart corrupts vsrc_0 pad, stalling stream 0 permanently
description: The 90s FPS watchdog calls schedule_stream_restart() on nvurisrcbin (stream 0). Cycling nvurisrcbin through NULL does not clean its dynamic vsrc_0 pad, so when it returns to PLAYING GStreamer emits 'Padname vsrc_0 is not unique'. After that, no video pad can be added and stream 0 is permanently stuck at 0fps despite nvurisrcbin's own reconnect still running. Fix: skip the NULL→PLAYING state cycle for nvurisrcbin streams; let built-in reconnect handle drops. Escalate to full service restart (loop.quit) only after 300s.
close_reason: Fixed in commit 3028c2b: track nvurisrcbin streams in gst_builder, skip destructive state-cycle restart for them, escalate to service restart after 300s instead

title: Filter werkzeug MJPEG probe noise from Sentry (HICON-R/HICON-D)
description: External scanner 192.168.175.254 hits the MJPEG HTTP port with TLS ClientHello and HTTP/0.9 payloads. werkzeug logs these malformed requests at ERROR level (mjpeg_server.py:437 setLevel(ERROR) does not filter ERROR records), so Sentry LoggingIntegration ships them as issues HICON-R/HICON-D. Fix: drop logger=='werkzeug' events in sentry_config._before_send. Zero functional impact; pure noise.
close_reason: Added logger=='werkzeug' drop in sentry_config._before_send; verified werkzeug 400 dropped while real errors kept

value: CORRECTED 2026-06-12: The '300s irreducible camera hardware cycle' conclusion was WRONG. Actual root cause: camera 0's default gateway was set to 192.168.28.1 which DOES NOT EXIST on the network (ARP incomplete forever). Hikvision firmware's periodic gateway health check failed every cycle and its recovery action bounced the camera's network/streaming stack every ~298.5s (free-running timer), silently killing all RTSP sessions (later RST win0 = TCP state lost), with 0-9s ICMP/HTTP blip. Camera OS never rebooted (uptime 5.6d). Controls: identical cameras 1&2 (same model/firmware) point at gateway 192.168.27.1 which EXISTS and never cycled. Also explains why replacing CP Plus with Hikvision didn't help (same dead gateway on 28.x). The old '95s TCP refusal' no longer applied by June (new TCP accepted within seconds). FIX (2026-06-12 19:09): gateway changed to 192.168.28.8 (NVR-1, always-on, answers ARP) via ISAPI PUT + camera reboot. Verification: watch [RTSP-OUTAGE] in pipeline.log for 30+ min.

rtspsrc path for stream 0 (HICON_USE_NVURISRCBIN_0=false) crashes with pgie-pouring: not-negotiated when first frame arrives from camera (~1.3s after PLAYING). Root cause: nvtracker rejects dynamic CAPS event during PLAYING state — caps on pgie_pouring→tracker_0 link aren't pre-established before data flows, unlike nvurisrcbin where vsrc_0 pad connects during PAUSED→PLAYING. Confirmed by: bypass tracker → no crash. Attempted fixes that failed: (1) deep-element-added to set do-rtsp-keep-alive on internal src element (ignored by nvurisrcbin), (2) batched-push-timeout=30s (irrelevant, crash is on first real frame not empty batch), (3) capsfilter(NV12+1600x900) between pgie and tracker (breaks displayq0→nvosd_0 link), (4) capsfilter(NV12 only) between pgie and tracker (same link failure). Next approach: use nvvideoconvert between caps0 and premuxq0 to output RGBA and match standard DeepStream sample pipeline topology, OR send RECONFIGURE event on tracker sink pad after PLAYING.

ai_vision/.env is gitignored and NOT in any backup/commit; if lost the pipeline crash-loops with 'No streams enabled - cannot create pipeline' (RTSP_STREAM_0/1/2 have no config.py defaults). Reconstructed 2026-06-09 from CLAUDE.md+memory. Critical non-default overrides .env MUST carry: HICON_USE_NVURISRCBIN_0/1/2=true (default false), HICON_STREAM_0_ANALYSIS_PROBE_ENABLED=false (default true -> segfault), HICON_RTSP_PROTOCOL_0=tcp. A backup now lives at ai_vision/.env.prod.bak.

Inference recording (HICON_ENABLE_INFERENCE_VIDEO=true) on the pyrometer stream (Stream 1) breaks its nvinfer branch: the recording tee triggers 'nvvideoconvert buffer transform failed' -> 'pgie-pyrometer: Internal data stream error (-5)', pyrometer inference gets paused and Stream 1 drops to 0 fps while Streams 0/2 stay healthy. Camera (192.168.27.253) and RTSP feed are fine (pings, ffprobe HEVC 1280x720@25). Fix: disable recording on Stream 1 via HICON_ENABLE_INFERENCE_VIDEO_STREAM_1=false (or globally). Pouring cameras 0/2 record fine. Confirmed 2026-06-09.

Mould-split env params (HICON_MOULD_SPLIT_MIN_DX_PX/MIN_DY_PX/DOM_RATIO/AXIS_ONLY_MIN_MAG/COOLDOWN_S/REARM_DX_PX/REARM_DY_PX/REARM_BASELINE_S) are VESTIGIAL/dead config. The running Python pouring_processor.py is a conversion of the C++ app DeepStream_Pipeline/apps/pouring/deepstream_pouring_app.cpp, which has NONE of these gate params. Python reads/scales/logs them but the split decision (_split_segment_by_motion, ~line 1252) uses ONLY self.displacement_thresh (Euclidean dist > threshold, sustained N frames). No quadrant guard / cooldown / rearm is live; CLAUDE.md's description of those is stale. Removed from .env 2026-06-09. The REAL split knobs (config.py defaults, NOT in .env): HICON_MOULD_DISPLACEMENT=0.15 and CLUSTER_BACKTRACK_CID_GUARD=5 — these intentionally diverge from the C++ source-of-truth (D_SPLIT=0.25, guard=1) as deliberate Hikvision re-tunes (user-confirmed, keep). r_merge effectively 0.07 (matches C++); the logged r_merge_x/y=0.08 are display-only.

Stream 0 analysis probe (HICON_STREAM_0_ANALYSIS_PROBE_ENABLED): setting to true causes segfault — the Python analysis probe calls pyds.get_nvds_buf_surface() on the NV12 analysis branch buffer while the main path (nvosd/nvinfer) is still accessing the same shared NVMM buffer on a different thread → IOMMU conflict on Jetson (same issue C++ plugin explicitly avoids). Leave false. Pouring runs via main-path CPU analysis fallback (osd_sink_pad_probe_stream0, update_main_path=True). Root cause of original gap: interval=1 (commit 7cc442b, 2026-05-01) halved detection rate from 25fps to 12.5fps, making brief ladle-mouth detection windows (~5s) miss the 25-frame accumulation threshold. Fix: interval=0 restored in config_pouring_pgie.txt.

Mould-count logic — TRUE current state (HEAD ff67860, verified 2026-06-09): SPLIT = _split_segment_by_motion using single displacement threshold (HICON_MOULD_DISPLACEMENT=0.15) sustained N frames; no quadrant/cooldown/rearm. CLUSTERING = baseline fixed r_cluster=0.08/r_merge=0.07 PLUS dynamic _rescue_refine_clusters (pouring_processor.py:1341-1407, called at ~1457) — adaptive per-cluster local radius (local_r=clamp(typical_x_gap*0.40), local_r_merge=local_r*0.35), fires ONLY on over-collapsed heats (valid_segs>=18, baseline/segs<=0.65, gap>=8). This rescue-clustering is the 'dynamic clustering' and is LIVE. PHYSICAL MOULD COUNT REDUCER (PHYSICAL_* cadence rules + _grouping_count, added in 42ba677/1c79351) was REMOVED by revert d633ea5 (May 14) which over-reached its 'revert v3 placement detector' title and also deleted config.py PHYSICAL_* (-29), heat_cycle_manager hook (-40), and tests/test_physical_mould_count_reducer.py (-85). Removal is INTENTIONAL/accepted — reducer NOT required (user-confirmed 2026-06-09). docs/Physical_Mould_Count_Logic.md is now an ORPHANED/stale doc describing removed code. NOTE: a transcript-mining subagent wrongly claimed the reducer was 'committed and active' — it is not.

Stream 0 RTSP drops root cause (confirmed 2026-05-04): gst_builder.py was silently overriding tcp→auto (UDP multi) for nvurisrcbin on stream 0, despite HICON_RTSP_PROTOCOL_0=tcp. UDP has no retransmission so any backpressure/packet loss killed the session. Fix: HICON_STREAM_0_NVURISRCBIN_RESPECT_CONFIGURED_PROTOCOL=true in .env. Confirmed by 3-soak proof (baseline=drops, force-tcp=0 outages in 330s). All the camera-side theories (300s firmware timer, bitrate, audio, CH102 switch) were red herrings — the bug was in our own code.
